Listening script (the audio is coming soon; until then, read it aloud with a volunteer at a normal, friendly speed):
Narrator: Lesson two. Marisol is at a leasing office. She wants to rent an apartment, and Mr. Chen helps her.
Mr. Chen: Good afternoon. Welcome to Park View Apartments. How can I help you?
Marisol: Hi. I'm here about the two-bedroom apartment. I want to fill out an application.
Mr. Chen: Great. Let's do it together. What's your current address?
Marisol: It's 418 Elm Street, apartment 3.
Mr. Chen: And how long have you lived there?
Marisol: I've lived there for two years.
Mr. Chen: OK. And your previous address?
Marisol: Before that, I lived on Lake Road with my cousins. I lived there for three years.
Mr. Chen: Why are you moving?
Marisol: My apartment is too small. My mother is going to live with me.
Mr. Chen: I see. Now, your job. Who's your employer?
Marisol: Green Valley Clinic. I'm a medical assistant.
Mr. Chen: How long have you worked there?
Marisol: Since March 2022. Before that, I worked at a bakery for two years.
Mr. Chen: And your start date at the clinic? March what?
Marisol: March fifteenth.
Mr. Chen: Thank you. We also need one reference. Not a family member, please.
Marisol: Can I give my supervisor's name? She's known me since I started.
Mr. Chen: Sure, that's fine. And will you have a roommate?
Marisol: No, just my mother. When can we move in?
Mr. Chen: The apartment is ready on June first. The lease is for one year.
Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

Round 2 (6 min): At the Leasing Office (pairs). A is the agent and asks the questions on the role card. B is the applicant and answers (invented answers are fine). A fills in the application form. Then switch. Each click shows the next step.
Role card questions: What's your current address? • How long have you lived there? • What's your previous address? • How long did you live there? • Who's your employer? • What's your position? • What's your start date? • Who's your reference? • Will you have a roommate? Useful: Can you spell that, please? • Is that with an e or an i? • Sorry, how long?
Spelling and numbers: the agent asks Can you spell that? Encourage learners to say street numbers in pairs: 418 = "four eighteen." A real rental application often asks for 3–5 years of addresses and a reference who is not family. Learners can write N/A (not applicable) when a line doesn't fit them.
5 or fewer: pairs or one group of 3. Every answer needs a reason; every partner asks a follow-up. Walk around and listen. Note 2 good sentences to praise and 1 common error for next week.
If behind: round 1 only.

Example on the board: I've lived in this city for four years. I moved here in 2022. I moved here because my sister lives here. With 5 or fewer, a learner can say it to you first and then write it.
